approachQuestion.prompt: Range totals for a monitoring console. A console receives one fixed sequence of n signed measurements and then q requests for inclusive index ranges. For each request [left, right], return the sum of the measurements at every index from left through right, including both endpoints. Example: measurements [5, −2, 4, 1] with requests [0,2], [1,3], [2,2] produce [7, 3, 4]. Which approach handles the whole batch correctly and efficiently?
constraints: Every request satisfies 0 ≤ left ≤ right < n; ranges are inclusive and may overlap or repeat.
The sequence is fixed for all q requests, is not modified, and all sums fit in signed 64-bit integers.
The output contains q sums in request order. Preparing reusable information before answering requests is allowed.

options.text: Build a cumulative array P of length n + 1 with P[0] = 0 and P[i + 1] = P[i] + measurements[i]. For each inclusive request [left, right], return P[right + 1] − P[left].
options.feedback: The leading zero makes the same subtraction work when a range begins at index zero; adding one to the right endpoint includes that endpoint.

options.text: For every request, walk from left through right and add those measurements directly, without preparing shared data.
options.feedback: This returns the right sum for every valid range, but repeatedly adds values from overlapping ranges. The same cumulative information can serve more than one request.

options.text: Build P with P[0] = 0, then answer [left, right] as P[right] − P[left].
options.feedback: The subtraction omits the value at right and also gives zero for a one-element range at index zero. For measurements [6, −2, 5] and request [0, 0], it returns 0 instead of 6.

options.text: Sort the measurements once, then use cumulative sums in the sorted sequence to answer the original index ranges.
options.feedback: A range is defined by positions in the received sequence. Sorting changes which values those positions contain; for [2, 7, −4], request [0, 0] must return 2, while either ascending or descending sort puts a different value first.

feedback.reason: The sequence is reused across many range requests, so separate the one-time preparation from answering each request. Inclusive endpoints require a deliberate prefix-array boundary convention.

details.rangeConvention: P[k] is the sum of indices 0 through k−1; therefore an inclusive [left, right] uses P[right+1]−P[left].
details.preparationVersusQueries: The sequence is fixed while q requests are answered; preparing once avoids rescanning overlapping ranges.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the prefix-array method described after the first answer, choose its tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair in terms of n measurements and q requests.

options.text: O(n + q) time and O(n) auxiliary space
O(nq) time and O(n) auxiliary space
O(n + q) time and O(1) auxiliary space
O(n log n + q) time and O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: The cumulative array is filled in one pass, then each of the q requests uses two stored prefix values and a subtraction. The array stores n+1 sums.

details.expectedPair: O(n + q) time; O(n) auxiliary space
details.timeDerivation: Building P visits each measurement once. Answering q requests performs constant work per request, for n + q total work.
details.spaceDerivation: P stores n+1 cumulative values. The output array is the required result and is excluded from auxiliary space; the supplied measurements and requests are input and are also excluded.
details.integerModel: All prefix and range sums fit signed 64-bit integers by the task constraints.
details.boundaryCheck: P[0]=0; [0,0] is P[1]−P[0], while [left,right] always includes right through P[right+1].
details.methodComparison: The target builds cumulative boundaries once and reuses them. Directly summing every requested range revisits values shared by overlapping ranges and can take O(nq) total time. Sorting changes the meaning of the original indices, and using P[right]−P[left] omits the inclusive right endpoint. The selected target uses O(n+q) time and O(n) auxiliary space, while the direct-scan alternative uses O(nq) worst-case time and O(1) auxiliary space.

methodReveal.title: Prepare cumulative boundaries once
methodReveal.description: Create P with a zero at the front. At each position, store the previous cumulative total plus the current measurement. A requested inclusive range is the cumulative total just after its right endpoint minus the total just before its left endpoint. This also handles a range starting at zero without a special case.
